title: Quantitative DFT+DMFT description of spectra and transport in the moderately correlated metal SrVO$_3$
abstract: A quantitative, material-specific account of spectral and transport properties remains a central challenge in the theory of strongly correlated materials. Combining density functional theory with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT) has proven to be a powerful approach for treating electron correlation effects and material specificity on an equal footing. Here, we examine the single-particle spectra and the dc and optical conductivity of SrVO$_3$, a prototypical, moderately correlated metal, within this framework. The degenerate $t_{2g}$ active space of SrVO$_3$, together with its well-established Fermi-liquid behavior, admits an effective-mass description governed by a single quasiparticle weight, yielding a nearly universal picture of the low-frequency, low-temperature regime. Employing a computationally efficient, real-frequency multi-orbital iterative perturbation theory (MO-IPT) impurity solver, we find reasonable agreement with experimental measurements of dc resistivity and optical conductivity across the entire experimentally relevant $(ω, T)$ range within a single, unified scheme. The agreement is shown to not depend on specific interaction parameters provided the quasiparticle weight is kept constant. These results indicate that, in SrVO$_3$, the $\mathbf{k}$-dependence of the self-energy may be weak, and vertex corrections may not dominate the dc and optical transport in this material.
summary: This paper applies the powerful DFT+DMFT method to study the electronic and transport properties of SrVO3, a moderately correlated metal. By using an advanced MO-IPT solver, the authors achieve quantitative agreement between theory and experiment for both resistivity and optical conductivity across various conditions. The work demonstrates that low-energy physics in this material is well-described by quasiparticle coherence within the $t_{2g}$ manifold.
main_problem: The central challenge is achieving a quantitative, material-specific description of both spectral and transport properties in strongly correlated materials.
main_result: The DFT+DMFT framework successfully provides a unified scheme showing good agreement between calculated observables (resistivity, optical conductivity) and experimental measurements for SrVO3 across relevant temperature and frequency ranges.
method: The study combines Density Functional Theory with Dynamical Mean-Field Theory ($	ext{DFT}+	ext{DMFT}$), utilizing a real-frequency multi-orbital iterative perturbation theory ($	ext{MO-IPT}$) solver.
model_or_system: The system is SrVO3, treated as a prototypical, moderately correlated metal whose low-energy physics is governed by the degenerate $t_{2g}$ active space. The calculation uses a Wannier-projected multi-orbital Hubbard model derived from DFT inputs.
key_observables: Single-particle spectra, dc resistivity ($ho$), and optical conductivity ($\sigma(\omega)$).
important_parameters: The low-frequency, low-temperature regime; the quasiparticle weight is noted as a key parameter governing the low-energy physics.
main_assumptions: Approximations include neglecting vertex corrections for transport calculations and using the single-site DMFT approximation. The $	ext{MO-IPT}$ solver avoids analytical continuation to real frequencies.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for quantitative theory, details the DFT+DMFT methodology (including Wannierization and MO-IPT), presents calculations of spectral functions and transport properties ($ho$, $\sigma(\omega)$) for SrVO3, and concludes by interpreting the agreement with experiment.
why_interesting: While focused on solids, the rigorous application of advanced many-body techniques like DMFT to predict measurable quantities (like optical response) provides a model for understanding strongly interacting quantum systems whose dynamics are governed by local correlations.

[10, 54] (green and blue symbols), measured below 20 K.

FIG. 3. Comparison of the measured dc resistivity of ul- traclean SrVO3 (green circles) with the calculated resistiv- ity (plus symbols), showing good agreement over the entire temperature range. The upper inset replots the same data on a log–log scale to emphasize the low-temperature behav- ior. The lower inset decomposes the calculated resistivity into electron–electron (e–e, dashed line) and electron–phonon (e– ph, dash–dot–dot line) contributions, together with the to- tal resistivity (solid line). The two scattering mechanisms contribute equally near ∼80 K, marking the crossover from electron–electron- to electron–phonon-dominated transport.
